title: Ephemeral latency sampling diary — seqmix epoch 02
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, daily-style diary capturing the seqmix / ephemeral sampling experiments we ran to isolate intermittent latency spikes seen in the last two sprints. Goal: produce a reproducible sampling methodology, capture transient signals, and land a small mitigation (config toggle + telemetry) for the next hotfix.

Context and motivation:
- Intermittent 95th/99th percentile spikes observed in production (customer tier C) during mixed short/long sequence workloads.
- Recent changes: fallback kernel selector (PR 4270) + prefix cache eviction tuning. Hypothesis space: cache churn, kernel selection latency, and rare contention on our async I/O path.
- Prior runs (shadow and smoke) were noisy; decided to do controlled seqmix epochs with deterministic seeds + pinned model variants to reduce variables.

Experimental setup (seqmix-epoch-02):
- Cluster: d-dedicated-rtg-4 (4xA100), stable infra image 2026-02-18, kernel runtime v2.8.3.
- Model: rwd-13b-q4f (pinned to v2026-02-10), KV cache enabled, intra-op threads pinned to 8.
- Load driver: bench-driver v1.14, mix generator script: tools/seqmix/generate.py (seed=20260225).
- Workload mix: 70% short (<64 tokens), 25% mid (64-512), 5% long (512-2048). QPS target: 420 steady-state with 25% burst windows (2s every 60s).
- Observability: p99/p995 with 1s resolution, CPU/GPU utilization, NVLINK counters, async-I/O latency histogram.
- Three runs: cold (after fresh deploy), warm (30m steady), hotburst (sustained 20m with 2x qps).

Day-by-day notes:
2026-02-25 (initial collection)
- Ran cold-start pass. Noted a 1.8x bump in tail latency during first 3 minutes (expected warmup).
- Unexpected 2x spike at ~9:12 into run correlated with NVLINK retrain event (see infra logs). Marked as infra-noise; dropped from comparison set.
- Saving raw traces: srun-seqmix02-cold-20260225.tar.gz (internal:/traces/seqmix02/).

2026-02-26 (isolation):
- Focused on cache eviction behavior. Modified prefix_cache_ttl from 600->900 and disabled async kv eviction for run 2.
- Outcome: median latency unchanged, 95th reduced by ~6%, but tail (p995) still had isolated outliers at ~5-7s.
- Hypothesis: outliers are not pure cache misses — look for contention in async writer.

2026-03-02 (contention test):
- Instrumented async write path to emit sampling span ids for any write > 50ms. Instrumentation PR: /pull/4281.
- Run results: majority of long async writes associated with large KV-miss fanout triggered by long sequences (>=1024). Matches pattern where a single long request causes multiple eviction+write subcalls.
- Notable: a small percentage (~0.07% of requests) produced writes that blocked the event-loop for >120ms and coincided with p995 spikes.

2026-03-05 (kernel selector A/B):
- Deployed A/B to route 10% traffic to alternative kernel selection heuristics (favor smaller-op kernels for mixed sequences).
- Result: A-group saw slightly higher median (due to worse micro-ops for long sequences) but lower p99.5 for short/mid sequences. Suggests kernel selector contributes to tail in heterogeneous mixes.

2026-03-08 (combined mitigation run):
- Applied two mitigations: async-writer backpressure cap (limit concurrent writes per worker to 4) + conservative kernel fallback for mix-heavy queues.
- Warm run at target QPS: p99 down ~12%, p995 down ~18% compared to baseline epoch 01. Tail still has rare >2s outliers but frequency reduced by ~60%.

Key observations and artifacts:
- Outliers strongly correlate with long-sequence fanout into the KV write path. Sequence mixing increases probability of a long request hitting during a burst, producing multi-step write activity that can block worker threads temporarily.
- Kernel selector can nudge tail behavior depending on long-regime performance characteristics — helpful to bias for short-heavy lanes.
- Backpressure cap reduced the severity/frequency of event-loop stalls but introduced a small increase in 50th percentile under extreme burst (tradeoff acceptable).

Repro commands (how to rerun locally / in CI):
- generate seqmix: python tools/seqmix/generate.py --seed 20260225 --out seqmix-epoch02.json
- run bench: bench-driver run --config experiments/seqmix-epoch02.yaml --note seqmix-02-runA --collect-traces
- collect traces: scripts/collect-traces --run seqmix-02-runA --dest s3://redwood-test/seqmix02/

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we change default kernel selector policy for mixed queues, or expose a per-route knob? (product input required)
- Investigate further: can KV write fanout be batched more aggressively for long sequences to amortize cost? (Ravi to spike)
- Add a lightweight telemetry tag to mark requests that triggered async write > 50ms so we can correlate with customer-facing traces. (Marta)
- SLO impact analysis: quantify cost vs latency tradeoff if we permanently cap concurrent writes. (Evan)

Suggested next steps (short-term):
- Ship conservative mitigation (backpressure cap + kernel bias) behind feature flag to a small portion of production (canary 5%) for 2 weeks.
- Add the write-duration telemetry tag and a dashboard showing correlation of tagged requests with route-level tail latency.
- Schedule follow-up: "seqmix review + product sync" on 2026-03-17 (15m) to decide on per-route knob vs global policy.

Meeting notes (2026-03-09 sync):
- Quick summary of runs and improvement numbers.
- Product asks for a concise one-pager showing customer impact and rollback plan. Action: Aisha to draft by 2026-03-12.
- Ops asked for an emergency rollback play if backpressure causes throughput regressions; added to runbook draft.

Appendix (raw numbers snapshot):
- Baseline epoch01 (warm): p50 28ms, p95 140ms, p99 420ms, p995 980ms
- seqmix-epoch02 (combined mitigation, warm): p50 30ms, p95 132ms, p99 370ms, p995 810ms
- Notes: minor median bump is consistent with tradeoff for lower tail.

Files produced / saved locations:
- traces: internal:/traces/seqmix02/srun-seqmix02-*.tar.gz
- dashboards: internal:/dashboards/seqmix-epoch02-latency
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4281 (async-writer spans), https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4290 (backpressure cap)

Author notes (short):
- This diary is intentionally terse and focused on reproducible steps and observable signals. The next iteration should fold results into a short one-pager for product and a longer postmortem if the canary shows customer impact.

-- Aisha
